item.title: 北朝鮮、地雷爆発巡り韓国に「代償払わせる」 責任転嫁と非難
item.description: [ソウル ３０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ソウル ３０日 ロイター] - 北朝鮮は３０日、非武装地帯（ＤＭＺ）で韓国人兵士が負傷した地雷爆発について、韓国が責任を北朝鮮側に転嫁したことに「代償を払わせる」と表明し、韓国側が北朝鮮軍に向けて発砲した場合は報復すると警告した。朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）が伝えた。

韓国の姜信哲国防相は２９日、ＤＭＺで先週発生した爆発は北朝鮮の地雷によるものだと述べ、朝鮮戦争の休戦協定に違反するものであり、北朝鮮への対応が必要だとした。

韓国は、朝鮮戦争の休戦協定を監督する国連軍司令部と共同でこの爆発を調査している。

北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記の妹である金与正党総務部長はＫＣＮＡを通じて発表した声明で、「韓国は責任を転嫁した上で、それを裏付ける『物的証拠』をでっち上げようとしている」と非難し、「挑発の首謀者は、自ら仕組んだ茶番の代償を払う覚悟をすべきだ」と警告した。

また、北朝鮮軍がＤＭＺの中央を通る軍事境界線を越えたことは一度もないと主張した。

韓国側は、北朝鮮兵が要塞化作業を行う中で境界線を越えた形跡があるとの見方を示している。

item.title: North Korea says South Korea to pay a price for shifting blame for mine blast, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea said on Wednesday that South Korea will pay a price for shifting the blame to Pyongyang for a mine blast that wounded two South Koreans at the Demilitarized Zone border and warned it will retaliate if the South opens fire on its troops.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea said on Wednesday that South Korea will pay a price for shifting the blame to Pyongyang for a mine blast that wounded two South Koreans at the Demilitarized Zone border and warned it will retaliate if the South opens fire on its troops. South Korea's [USN:L1N45L07A TEXT:"defence minister"] said on Tuesday that North Korean mines caused a blast last week and that it would take "corresponding" action. Kang Shin-chul also said North Korea likely planted mines as part of fortifying the border. South Korea together with the UN Command that oversees the Korean War armistice have been conducting a probe over the blast that on September 21 wounded two South Korean personnel of a team on a reconnaissance mission inside the 4-kilometre- (2.49-mile) wide DMZ. "The tribes of South Korea are trying to fabricate 'material evidence' for proving it after shifting the blame for the incident onto the other," the North Korean leader's sister, Kim Yo Jong, said in a statement issued on the KCNA official news agency. Kim is considered an influential confidant of her brother and often speaks publicly on external matters. "Ringleaders of provocation should be prepared for paying a price for the farce of their own making," she said. "It is too low and dirty as befitting the tribes of South Korea," she said. "Such a farce is by no means new." She also said North Korean troops have never crossed the Military Demarcation Line that runs through the centre of the DMZ. South Korea has said it believes there are signs North Korean soldiers breached the border line as it conducted fortification work. North Korea has ramped up hostility toward the South in recent years, saying it no longer seeks unification as a national goal and that Seoul was its "primary foe."

item.title: Canada will do all it can to ensure Cleveland-Cliffs meets obligations, Carney says
item.description: Canada will ensure that Cleveland-Cliffs meets its obligations after it announced plans to idle some production at an Ontario steel plant, putting hundreds of workers out of a job, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada will ensure that Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF.N) meets its obligations after it announced plans to [USN:L1N45K0T7 TEXT:"idle"] some production at an Ontario steel plant, putting hundreds of workers out of a job, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday. "The company made representations and has legal obligations for employment. We intend to use all the powers that we have and pursue them to the full extent of the law," Carney told reporters in Vancouver. He did not give details.

item.title: Trump releases AI accord with tech executives
item.description: President Donald Trump released a document on Tuesday that his administration cast as an accord on artificial intelligence and which he said earlier was signed by him and tech executives that he met in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump released a document on Tuesday that his administration cast as an accord on artificial intelligence and which he said earlier was signed by him and tech executives that he [USN:L6N45L0Q5 TEXT:"met in Washington"]. Trump released the one-page document on his Truth Social platform - which he had earlier described as "morally binding" - and that urged four layers of controls in companies: It asked companies to partner with an external auditor or evaluator to carry out independent assessments of whether a company's AI control and monitoring systems were operating as intended. It urged companies to designate an independent committee of the board of directors to oversee and receive reports from internal and external auditors and from teams operating AI controls. It asked for internal controls to monitor capabilities and alignment of AI models during training and deployment around areas like cybersecurity, biosecurity and chemical threats to ensure that models "do not hack or access technical systems in unintended ways." The accord asked companies to have an internal team to ensure "all of the controls, monitoring and detection are operating as intended." MORE DETAILS AND QUOTES: The document was signed by Trump and the bosses of Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, social media platform X and NVIDIA. "Over time, it may make sense to codify these steps into laws or regulations. Regardless of whether this is required of companies, we believe that implementing these controls and audits is critical to ensuring a safe future for everyone, and each of our companies are committed to doing this," the White House accord said. "The participating companies will meet regularly to establish standards and best practices to improve the safety of their systems," it added.

item.title: Brasil supera las previsiones y crea 165.827 empleos formales en agosto
item.description: Brasil generó 165.827 empleos formales el mes pasado, una cifra superior a todas las estimaciones de una encuesta de analistas de Bloomberg, donde la previsión media apuntaba a 106.900 nuevos puestos ...
item.dc:creator: Beatriz Reis
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La mayor economía de América Latina creó más empleos de lo esperado en agosto, lo que le brindó al presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva un dato económico positivo a pocos días de que los votantes acudan a las urnas. Ver más: Lula no logra ampliar su ventaja sobre Bolsonaro a días de las elecciones en Brasil Brasil generó 165.827 empleos formales el mes pasado, una cifra superior a todas las estimaciones de una encuesta de analistas de Bloomberg , donde la previsión media apuntaba a 106.900 nuevos puestos de trabajo para agosto. Según datos gubernamentales publicados el martes, los sectores de servicios y construcción representaron la mayor parte de las contrataciones. El mercado laboral brasileño se ha mantenido bastante resistente, incluso cuando la economía en general pierde impulso, y el bajo desempleo y los salarios estables proporcionan a Lula un contexto relativamente favorable de cara a la primera vuelta. No obstante, el panorama económico general es menos tranquilizador. El crecimiento está perdiendo impulso y la inflación se aceleró más de lo esperado a principios de septiembre, lo que complica el esfuerzo del presidente en funciones por convencer a los votantes de que su situación financiera está mejorando, a pesar de las medidas gubernamentales destinadas a proteger a los hogares de los elevados costos de financiación y del aumento de los precios del petróleo. Ver más: Lula enfrenta desgaste y lucha por cada voto en el noreste de Brasil, su mayor bastión electoral Esas señales contradictorias también complican el próximo paso del banco central. Los responsables de la política monetaria, encabezados por Gabriel Galípolo, recortaron la tasa Selic por quinta reunión consecutiva en septiembre, hasta el 13,75%, pero ofrecieron pocas indicaciones sobre lo que vendrá a continuación, reiterando que el ritmo y la magnitud de cualquier nueva flexibilización dependerán de los datos que se vayan conociendo. Ahora, las elecciones se convierten en otra variable. Los brasileños votan el 4 de octubre en una reñida contienda entre Lula y el candidato conservador Flávio Bolsonaro, y los inversores están atentos no solo a quién gana, sino también a cómo reaccionan los mercados, en particular el real. Una fuerte caída tras las elecciones podría reducir el margen de maniobra del banco central para seguir recortando las tasas de interés, mientras que una reacción moderada podría abrir la puerta a nuevas medidas de flexibilización monetaria. --Con la colaboración de Giovanna Serafim. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Knicks undecided on White House visit
item.description: The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks have not decided whether to visit the White House and President Donald Trump this season, according to coach Mike Brown on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks have not decided whether to visit the White House and President Donald Trump this season, according to coach Mike Brown on Tuesday. If the Knicks go to D.C., they would be the first NBA champions to visit the White House during Trump's two terms. "No, it's still something that our guys, or the organization, is internally discussing and, you know, whatever we decide to do, we'll all do together," Brown told reporters at training camp. Knicks owner James Dolan, who hosted New York City native Trump for Game 3 of last season's NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden, said in June, after the team won the championship, that the White House had extended an invitation and the organization accepted it. The White House said it was in contact with the team and it "looked forward to hosting the team at a date to be determined in the near future." Trump was inaugurated in 2017 for his first four-year term and again in 2025 for his second. During that time, the Golden State Warriors (twice), Toronto Raptors, Los Angeles Lakers and Oklahoma City Thunder have won titles but have not visited the White House. Trump withdrew an invitation to the Warriors in 2017 after Stephen Curry expressed hesitation about attending, and the Lakers did not visit after their 2020 championship because of scheduling issues and COVID-19 restrictions. The Thunder said earlier this year that they could not visit because the timing did not work out. The Milwaukee Bucks, Warriors and Boston Celtics visited the White House during Joe Biden's presidency. The Denver Nuggets chose not to attend after their 2023 title, reportedly because of multiple scheduling conflicts and the Nuggets' desire to focus on securing the top seed in the Western Conference playoffs. --Field Level Media

item.title: Boeing wins US Navy's next-generation fighter contract, Pentagon says
item.description: Boeing has been selected to build the US Navy's next-generation stealth fighter, the Pentagon said on Tuesday, the aerospace company's second consecutive major win on fighter jets and capping months of delay over a program that is central to countering China in the Pacific.
item.dc:creator: Mike Stone
item.content:encoded: Boeing (BA.N) has been selected to build the US Navy's next-generation stealth fighter, the Pentagon said on Tuesday, the aerospace company's second consecutive major win on fighter jets and capping months of delay over a program that is central to countering China in the Pacific. Boeing beat out rival Northrop Grumman Corp (NOC.N) for the development contract, worth $20 billion, to produce test aircraft. The program could grow to hundreds of billions over its lifetime as production ramps up and, potentially, as international customers place orders. Boeing was also selected in March last year to build the Air Force's new stealthy F-47 fighter, giving it two marquee sixth-generation jet contracts in consecutive years. Boeing was viewed as a strong contender throughout the competition because of its long history building carrier-based fighters for the Navy, including the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet that the new fighter is designed to replace. That pedigree helped offset questions raised by defense officials about whether Boeing could field enough engineers and suppliers to execute both the F-47 and Navy fighter simultaneously — concerns that appear to have been resolved in the company's favor. Boeing shares were up 2.25% in extended trading on Tuesday, while Northrop shares were down 3.5%. ST. LOUIS PRODUCTION BOOST The contract is a significant boost for Boeing's fighter production operations in St. Louis, Missouri, which is shutting down the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet and EA-18G Growler production lines. Steve Parker, president and chief executive officer of Boeing Defense, Space & Security, said in a statement the company has made investments "in new facilities uniquely suited to build multiple products with next-generation capabilities, our dedicated and talented team is ready to execute this critical program." Currently designated the "F/A-XX" program, the new jet will be the centerpiece of the Navy's Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems. The jet "represents a crucial, non-negotiable investment in America’s national security and long-term air combat capabilities," Michael Duffey, the Pentagon's chief weapons buyer, said in a statement. DELAYS AND CONGRESSIONAL INTERVENTION Still, it has been buffeted by delays and funding disputes for years. Some Pentagon officials had sought to delay it by [USN:L1N3RL026 TEXT:"up to three years"], citing engineering and supply-chain capacity concerns, before Congress intervened, earmarking $750 million for the program in the 2025 tax-cut and spending law and an additional $1.4 billion in fiscal 2026. Lockheed Martin Corp (LMT.N) was [USN:S0N3OV0A2 TEXT:"eliminated"] from the competition in March 2025 after Navy officials determined its design had not met required criteria, leaving Boeing and Northrop as the finalists. With China rapidly fielding advanced combat aircraft, including designs Beijing describes as sixth-generation, the Navy has faced pressure to move quickly or risk operating without a modern carrier-based fighter in the 2030s and beyond. The new jet is expected to feature advanced stealth capabilities, improved range and endurance, and the ability to integrate with uncrewed combat aircraft and the Navy's carrier-based air defense systems. The Navy still plans to buy more than 270 Lockheed Martin F-35C jets for its carrier fleet, which will fly alongside the F/A-XX once it enters service. First production F/A-XX jets are expected in the 2030s, while the Super Hornet fleet, in service since the 1990s, is expected to remain flying into the 2040s.

item.title: Trump says he is embarking on 32 days of campaign travel before November elections
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he plans 32 days of campaign travel ahead of the November midterm elections, putting himself and his record at the center of Republicans' fight to hold on to Congress as polls show Democrats poised for gains.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he plans 32 days of campaign travel ahead of the November midterm elections , putting himself and his record at the center of Republicans' fight to hold on to Congress as polls show Democrats poised for gains. The November 3 elections will decide whether Republicans retain control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate or whether Democrats gain the power to shape Trump's final two years in office, including through investigations into his administration. Many polls show Democrats leading in key House races and challenging for control of the Senate as well, as Americans fret about high gasoline prices and Trump's ongoing war with Iran . But Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House, projected confidence about his party's prospects and dismissed signs that some Republicans are distancing themselves from him in the final weeks of the campaign. "You love me, and I love them," he said, with Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson standing alongside him. Trump said he will soon embark on what he described as "literally a 32-day tour" of various states, including stops in Texas and Ohio this week. "Just so you understand, they all want me to go. I'm one person. They all want me to go campaign," he said. The flurry of campaigning comes later than the president's advisers initially had envisioned, after a White House calendar dominated for much of the year by foreign policy and the Iran conflict. Some Republican candidates have welcomed Trump's involvement, while others have emphasized local issues and their own records as they navigate difficult political terrain.

item.title: Bayer faces trial test of remaining Roundup claims after US Supreme Court win
item.description: Attorneys for three cancer patients told a Missouri jury on Tuesday that Bayer's Monsanto unit failed to adequately test its Roundup weedkiller before selling it, starting a trial that could help determine the viability of some Roundup lawsuits after a US Supreme Court ruling in Bayer's favor this year.
item.dc:creator: Dietrich Knauth
item.content:encoded: Attorneys for three cancer patients told a Missouri jury on Tuesday that Bayer's Monsanto unit failed to adequately test its Roundup weedkiller before selling it, starting a trial that could help determine the viability of some Roundup lawsuits after a US Supreme Court ruling in Bayer's favor this year. Bayer is facing approximately 65,000 claims in US state and federal courts from plaintiffs who say they developed cancer after using Roundup at home or on the job. The company is seeking to resolve nearly all existing and future claims through a $7.25 billion class action settlement that is [USN:L1N4520WJ TEXT:"under review"] by a Missouri state court judge in St. Louis. Tuesday's case before a different St. Louis judge involves three women who are not participating in the proposed settlement and are pursuing claims that Roundup was defectively designed and unsafe for sale, legal theories that the Supreme Court's June ruling did not directly address. Plaintiffs Theresa Aretino, Cynthia Fernandez and Betty Larkin used Roundup regularly and later developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and Fernandez died before the trial began, according to the women’s attorneys. "Monsanto did not adequately test Roundup," the plaintiffs’ attorney Greg Dovel said in opening statements on Tuesday. “To this day, they’ve never done all the testing they've needed to do." Bayer has denied the claims and said that decades of studies have shown glyphosate, Roundup's active ingredient, is safe and does not cause cancer. Reuters viewed the trial on Courtroom View Network. EARLY TEST The trial could provide an early indication of how courts and juries will treat design-defect and other claims that do not rely on allegations that Roundup's label failed to warn consumers about cancer risks. The litigation has weighed on Bayer since its 2018 acquisition of Monsanto, costing the company billions of dollars and driving down its share price. Bayer has argued that the design-defect claims are foreclosed by the [USN:S0N40Z03O TEXT:"US Supreme Court's ruling"] that barred lawsuits alleging that Roundup’s warning label failed to adequately warn consumers about cancer risks. The court said federal law requires herbicide makers to use the exact label approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency, and EPA has concluded that Roundup’s label does not require a cancer warning. Dovel told the jury on Tuesday that EPA’s review of Roundup's safety was outdated and based on incomplete science. The EPA is in the midst of a new review of glyphosate. It has estimated it will complete the re-evaluation by the end of 2026. "EPA approval of Roundup doesn’t mean that it is safe," Dovel said. Bayer's lawyer Paul Boehm told the jury the plaintiffs cannot prove that glyphosate-based herbicides are too dangerous to sell, because that argument contradicts decades of safety reviews by regulatory bodies worldwide, including the EPA.

item.title: Costarricense Grynspan, con ligera ventaja en carrera para ser secretaria general de la ONU: fuentes
item.description: Una votación informal celebrada el martes en el Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas situó a Rebeca Grynspan, ex vicepresidenta de Costa Rica, como la principal candidata en la carrera por convertirse en la nueva secretaria general de la entidad, informaron fuentes cercanas al proceso.
item.dc:creator: Antoni Slodkowski, David Brunnstrom
item.content:encoded: Una votación informal celebrada el martes en el Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas situó a Rebeca Grynspan, ex vicepresidenta de Costa Rica, como la principal candidata en la carrera por convertirse en la nueva secretaria general de la entidad, informaron fuentes cercanas al proceso. La cuarta votación secreta del Consejo de Seguridad, compuesto por 15 miembros, se celebró tras la reunión de líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General de Nueva York la semana pasada. La primera y la tercera votación, celebradas en julio y septiembre, también mostraron a Grynspan encabezando la carrera, mientras que otra en agosto situó a la embajadora de Guyana ante la ONU, Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, en el primer puesto. Tras la retirada de la carrera de la expresidenta chilena Michelle Bachelet este mes, siete candidatos compiten por suceder a António Guterres, quien dejará el cargo a finales de 2026 tras dos mandatos de cinco años. Todavía es posible que se sumen más candidatos a la carrera. En última instancia, los cinco miembros del Consejo de Seguridad con derecho a veto —Estados Unidos, China, Rusia, Francia y el Reino Unido— deben ponerse de acuerdo sobre un candidato. Cuando Guterres fue elegido en 2016, el Consejo necesitó seis votaciones indicativas para alcanzar un acuerdo. El Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU acabará recomendando formalmente a un candidato a la Asamblea General, integrada por 193 miembros, para su elección. La aprobación por parte de la Asamblea se ha considerado durante mucho tiempo un mero trámite.

item.title: Trump diz que não sabe se Irã vai “ceder já”
item.description: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta terça-feira que não sabe se o Irã vai “ceder já”, mas descreveu o país como estando se saindo “muito mal” em sua guerra contra os Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta terça-feira que não sabe se o Irã vai “ceder já”, mas descreveu o país como estando se saindo “muito mal” em sua guerra contra os Estados Unidos. DETALHES E DECLARAÇÕES: “Não sei se eles vão ceder já, mas vão ceder”, disse Trump aos repórteres. “Eles estão indo muito mal”, acrescentou. Um bloqueio dos EUA cortou a principal fonte de renda do Irã — as exportações de petróleo —, e os custos econômicos da guerra tornaram a vida mais difícil para os iranianos. O presidente do Irã disse à Assembleia Geral da ONU na semana passada que Teerã nunca se renderia à pressão dos EUA. O aumento dos preços do petróleo devido à guerra também se tornou uma questão importante para o Partido Republicano de Trump rumo às eleições de meio de mandato de novembro nos EUA. A guerra levou ao bloqueio do Estreito de Ormuz, por onde passava um quinto do abastecimento global de petróleo bruto e GNL antes do conflito. Trump tem apresentado metas e cronogramas variáveis para a guerra contra o Irã, que começou em 28 de fevereiro, quando os EUA e Israel atacaram o Irã e o governo iraniano respondeu com seus próprios ataques contra Israel e os países do Golfo Pérsico que abrigam bases norte-americanas. Os ataques dos EUA e de Israel ao Irã e os ataques israelenses ao Líbano mataram milhares de pessoas e deslocaram milhões.

item.title: Ceuta mass migrant crossing handling 'responsibility of all EU,' Spanish king says
item.description: European countries should have shown more solidarity and offered more support to Spain after the mass arrival in Ceuta of tens of thousands of migrants, Spanish King Felipe VI said on Tuesday during a gala dinner to mark a visit by French President Emmanuel Macron.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: European countries should have shown more solidarity and offered more support to Spain after the mass arrival in Ceuta of tens of thousands of migrants, Spanish King Felipe VI said on Tuesday during a gala dinner to mark a visit by French President Emmanuel Macron. In an unusually outspoken address reflecting the depth of the crisis facing Spain following the Ceuta [USN:L8N43W1SU TEXT:"border rush"] that took place two months ago on Wednesday, the king said what happened in the enclave on the North African coast was "unacceptable" and generated an enormous security, public order and humanitarian challenge. "It's a situation that ought to have as a consequence a reinforcement of collaboration between member states in resources and cooperation," he said. "The European countries that suffer the most pressure from being on the external borders of the European Union cannot alone bear a responsibility that also belongs to everyone." The king spoke during a dinner at the Royal Palace in Madrid also attended by Spain's Socialist prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, a rare European proponent of the benefits of migration who launched a mass regularisation of irregular migrants that concluded in the summer. Sanchez, however, has proposed possible [USN:L8N45L09S TEXT:"changes"] to asylum rules to return arrivals more quickly, which NGOs and lawyers say would violate human rights conventions. Asked in a news conference about the plans, territorial policy minister Angel Victor Torres said the government was "analysing the possibility" of a legislative amendment but that it was "not easy" due to questions of international law. Following the mass crossing of 72,000 migrants into Ceuta on July 30, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen commended Spain's swift action in returning most arrivals to Morocco. Other leaders were less understanding, however, with Italy [USN:L8N43X2N1 TEXT:"suspending"] the European Union's border-free Schengen arrangements with Spain for one month. European Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner unveiled a [USN:L8N45L0QW TEXT:"plan"] on Tuesday to strengthen EU border controls in the wake of Ceuta. The plan, which requires the approval of member states, would strengthen the mandate of Frontex, the EU border protection agency, and give it a standing corps ready for immediate deployment.

item.title: White & Case hires former DOJ antitrust chief Slater
item.description: Law firm White & Case said on Tuesday that Gail Slater, the former head of the US Justice Department’s antitrust division under President Donald Trump, will join as a partner based in Washington, D.C.
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Law firm White & Case said on Tuesday that Gail Slater, the former head of the US Justice Department’s antitrust division under President Donald Trump, will join as a partner based in Washington, D.C. Slater, a veteran antitrust attorney, [USN:S0N3YA05C TEXT:"stepped down"] from the Justice Department role in February amid a battle within the administration over policing anti-competitive conduct. She held the [USN:S0N3MF07C TEXT:"position"] for less than a year. Slater was not immediately made available for comment. In a statement provided by the firm, she called New York-founded White & Case “a great match for my practice.” She will join the firm's global antitrust practice and global technology industry group. She was an economic advisor to US Vice President JD Vance during his time in the Senate and served on the White House’s National Economic Council during Trump's first term. Slater also worked for a decade as an antitrust lawyer at the Federal Trade Commission, where she brought cases to block mergers including Whole Foods' acquisition of organic grocer Wild Oats, and did stints as an executive at Fox Corp and Roku. While Slater was at the helm of the antitrust division, the DOJ launched probes into [USN:L3N3QM1N9 TEXT:"egg producers"] and the [USN:FWN3WJ128 TEXT:"meatpacking industry"] last year, and required US power company Constellation Energy to [USN:L4N3XB1GF TEXT:"divest three power plants"] in order to complete its $16.4 billion acquisition of Calpine Corporation. Her division continued the US crackdown on Big Tech companies that started during Trump's first term, with major cases against Alphabet's Google and Apple. Reuters and other outlets reported in July 2025 that two of [USN:L6N3TQ0V5 TEXT:"Slater's deputies were fired"] for insubordination after Slater pushed back on orders to settle a case that would have blocked Hewlett Packard Enterprise's $14 billion acquisition of Juniper Networks. The move exposed a power struggle within the Trump administration between proponents of robust antitrust enforcement and dealmakers seeking to leverage influence. Slater joined the conservative think tank American Compass as competition and technology policy chair in March. Several large law firms over the past month have hired former top government officials to build out antitrust practices.

item.title: Saint Laurent goes for gold in Paris show that may be Vaccarello's finale
item.description: Saint Laurent creative director Anthony Vaccarello unveiled a head-to-toe gold collection of slinky dresses and textured tailoring at Paris Fashion Week on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: Saint Laurent creative director Anthony Vaccarello unveiled a head-to-toe gold collection of slinky dresses and textured tailoring at Paris Fashion Week on Tuesday. The spring/summer 2027 show marked 10 years since Vaccarello's first show for the Parisian label owned by luxury group Kering, and came amid reports he was set to step down from the role. On a raised runway under a giant gold chandelier, models strode past wearing gold dresses with raised embroidery, gold brocade skirts and jackets with sharp collars, and gold trench coats. The Eiffel Tower also glittered gold in the background of the show staged outdoors at the Trocadero fountain, with front-row guests including Blackpink singer Rosé, model Rosie Huntington-Whitely, and Oscar-winning actors Eddie Redmayne and Rami Malek. Black gowns with billowing sleeves and long trains were the final looks of the show, and Charlotte Gainsbourg performed a song in a classic Saint Laurent black suit before Vaccarello came out to applause from the crowd, smiling and waving. Vaccarello is credited with expanding Saint Laurent's reach. The brand's revenues were down 6% last year but Kering said in July that it had returned to growth in the first half.

item.title: US states take steps to curb diesel and gasoline prices
item.description: US states are taking a range of steps to curb diesel and gasoline prices that have soared in recent months due to supply disruptions stemming from the US war on Iran, Ukrainian strikes on Russia's refineries, and dwindling global inventories.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: US states are taking a range of steps to curb diesel and gasoline prices that have soared in recent months due to supply disruptions stemming from the US war on Iran , Ukrainian strikes on Russia's refineries, and dwindling global inventories. Diesel hit a record of $6.53 a gallon a week ago, according to AAA data. The Trump administration and Republican candidates in some of the tightest election races are looking for ways to bring down diesel prices without disrupting fuel supplies or creating additional costs elsewhere in the economy, as November's midterm elections approach and President Donald Trump's economic approval ratings remain under strain. The White House is considering regulatory relief that would allow broader sales of [USN:L1N45K0KX TEXT:"red-dyed diesel"], a move that could allow some buyers to avoid the federal fuel tax, while Trump said last week that he [USN:SPN45A01C TEXT:"backed"] a ban on diesel exports. Red-dyed diesel is generally reserved for off-road uses such as farming and is exempt from most federal fuel taxes. Many states have already started to take measures. Here are some of the steps states have taken so far: Alabama: Alabama last week said it would halt the enforcement of restrictions on use of red-dyed diesel for 120 days. California: The state on Monday suspended California’s seasonal summer-blend gasoline requirement for the remainder of the season and directed state agencies to allow winter-blend gasoline to be manufactured, imported, distributed, and sold in the state immediately. Georgia: Georgia on Monday suspended the state gasoline and diesel tax for 30 days and suspended weight restrictions on commercial vehicles to reduce the cost of transporting goods. Illinois: The state's governor paused a 1.3-cent increase in the gasoline tax for six months this summer. Indiana: The state suspended its sales tax on gasoline. Kentucky: In May, the governor signed an executive order reducing the gasoline tax by 10 cents, freezing any increases in gasoline taxes and any increases in motor vehicle property tax in 2027. Louisiana: The state last week said it would allow farmers and timber harvesters to use the dyed diesel fuel in highway vehicles. Massachusetts: The governor plans to file legislation to temporarily suspend its 24-cent-per-gallon tax on gasoline and diesel for two months beginning seven days after passage. Retailers would be required to reflect the temporary suspension in prices at the pump, and gasoline station owners would be protected from losing money on fuel sold at the reduced price. Michigan: The state's governor temporarily waived an environmental rule, allowing regional gasoline stations to sell cheaper, higher-vapor winter blends and E15 through the summer. Montana: The state waived certain hours-of-service rules for intrastate gasoline and diesel haulers. Nebraska: The state allowed highway-registered vehicles to use untaxed dyed diesel fuel without facing state fines or penalties. The governor also said that diesel taxes paid while transporting Nebraska's seasonally produced products and livestock on state roads are eligible for a refund and eased weight limits for seasonal crop transport. Oklahoma: The governor paused enforcement of all taxes, regulations, and fines levied on the use of red-dyed diesel in farm vehicles and in highway vehicles for 120 days. South Dakota: The state permitted farmers and haulers transporting crop, livestock, and other agricultural commodities to do so at up to 10% above standard highway weight limits and temporarily waived the $25 overweight trip permit fee. It also directed the department of revenue to monitor fuel supplies and determine if a tax refund to suppliers is warranted if regular diesel needs to be used in farm machinery because of potential shortages of dyed diesel. Texas: The governor said he would expand the use of dyed diesel on Texas roads, raised the allowable weight for fuel, agricultural and timber, and suspended the state's low-emission diesel fuel regulations to reduce emissions of nitrogen oxides from diesel-powered motor vehicles and non-road equipment.

item.title: US says two Indian nationals indicted in counterfeit Ozempic smuggling scheme
item.description: Two Indian nationals have been indicted by a US federal grand jury for allegedly smuggling and selling counterfeit Ozempic, the weight-loss drug, the Department of Justice said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two Indian nationals have been indicted by a US federal grand jury for allegedly smuggling and selling counterfeit Ozempic, the weight-loss drug, the Department of Justice said on Tuesday. One of the defendants, Swapnadip Roy, pleaded not guilty after being extradited from Italy while the other, Vicky Ramancha, remains at large, the department said. Between July 2023 and April 2024, Roy and Ramancha allegedly obtained counterfeit Ozempic in China and sold it to US distributors at discounted prices, it said. A legal representative for Roy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. One for Ramancha was not immediately available. The counterfeit medication included packaging, inserts and labels allegedly meant to convince purchasers that they were receiving authentic Ozempic, the popular weight-loss drug that can cost hundreds of dollars per month for patients. "The scheme continued even after the FDA seized some of the counterfeit Ozempic in December 2023 and issued a public warning regarding the products," the Justice Department said. Roy and Ramancha were charged with smuggling and selling counterfeit drugs, conspiracy to commit smuggling and to defraud the United States. They face up to 71 years in prison if convicted.

item.title: 米、イラン武器調達支援の13個人・団体に制裁 ロシアや中国など
item.description: [ワシントン ２９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２９日　ロイター] - 米政府は２９日、イランの武器・部品の調達を支援したとして、ロシア、中国、香港、パキスタンなどに拠点を置く計１３の個人・団体を制裁対象に追加した。財務省と国務省が発表した。

ベセント財務長官は「財務省は、イラン政権へのいかなる支援も容認せず、イランを支える者の特定、摘発、孤立化を継続する」と述べた。

財務省によると、今回の制裁はイランの兵器計画の再建能力を弱体化させると同時に、調達活動を支援する側のコストを引き上げることを目的としている。

item.title: Lamine marca doblete en victoria de España por Liga de Naciones, Inglaterra vence a República Checa
item.description: Lamine Yamal marcó dos goles y la selección española, campeona del mundo, amplió el martes su racha invicta a 40 partidos y mantuvo su inicio perfecto en el Grupo A3 de la Liga de Naciones con una victoria 4-1 en casa ante Croacia, mientras que Inglaterra se impuso 2-0 a República Checa en Praga.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamine Yamal marcó dos goles y la selección española, campeona del mundo, amplió el martes su racha invicta a 40 partidos y mantuvo su inicio perfecto en el Grupo A3 de la Liga de Naciones con una victoria 4-1 en casa ante Croacia, mientras que Inglaterra se impuso 2-0 a República Checa en Praga. En una reedición de la final de la Liga de Naciones de 2023, que España ganó en los penales, Croacia se recuperó tras encajar un gol tempranero y logró empatar, pero no pudo hacer frente a su rival en el global del encuentro. El primer partido en casa de España desde que ganó el Mundial en julio estuvo precedido por la exhibición del trofeo por parte de Rodri sobre el terreno de juego, y las celebraciones continuaron en Sevilla cuando Lamine abrió el marcador en el segundo minuto tras un centro de Alex Baena al área que Fermín López dejó pasar. Los visitantes empataron gracias a un cabezazo de Dion Beljo en el minuto 28, pero España tardó menos de tres minutos en recuperar la ventaja. Lamine envió un centro al área pequeña desde la banda derecha y Marc Pubill remató de cabeza con fuerza, superando a Livakovic. Lamine marcó el tercero de España en el minuto 63 tras un pase de Pedri, y el suplente Nico Williams sentenció la victoria con un gol en el minuto 89. "Ganar un Mundial, ya sabes lo que es, toda España vino a apoyarnos y espero que sigamos ganando y dándole alegrías a esta afición que se lo merece", dijo Williams tras el partido. "Muy feliz por los tres puntos, por contribuir a la victoria del equipo y este gol me sirve para coger confianza". En tanto, Inglaterra tuvo dificultades para superar a los checos en la primera parte pese a que su rival quedó con 10 hombres luego de que Pavel Sulc fuera expulsado en el minuto 23. Pero un gol de Anthony Gordon al comienzo de la segunda parte abrió el marcador para el equipo de Thomas Tuchel. Inglaterra logró el segundo gol en el minuto 69, gracias a que Harry Kane estaba en el lugar adecuado en el momento oportuno para aprovechar un balón suelto en el área y enviar su disparo al segundo palo.

item.title: Prospecto do IPO da Anthropic revela profunda dependência de grandes empresas de tecnologia como parceiras
item.description: O prospecto do IPO da Anthropic mostra o quanto a empresa depende de um pequeno grupo de clientes e gigantes da tecnologia, destacando os principais riscos para a desenvolvedora de IA, que pede aos investidores que apoiem seu ambicioso plano de capital intensivo, que, segundo ela, transformará a economia global.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O prospecto do IPO da Anthropic mostra o quanto a empresa depende de um pequeno grupo de clientes e gigantes da tecnologia, destacando os principais riscos para a desenvolvedora de IA, que pede aos investidores que apoiem seu ambicioso plano de capital intensivo, que, segundo ela, transformará a economia global. A empresa direcionou 47% de suas vendas para clientes no ano passado por meio de parceiros de nuvem, como a Amazon (AMZN.O) e o Google, da Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , de acordo com uma cópia de seu pedido confidencial de IPO vista pela Reuters. Essas duas empresas, que estão impulsionando a distribuição da desenvolvedora de IA e coletando as faturas dos clientes em seu nome, também são grandes investidoras da Anthropic, fornecedoras cruciais de poder computacional e concorrentes diretas em IA. A Amazon se recusou a comentar. A Anthropic e a Alphabet não responderam aos pedidos de comentários. O documento oferece um raro vislumbre do interior de uma empresa que praticamente não existia há alguns anos, mas que está crescendo a um ritmo vertiginoso devido ao seu papel fundamental no desenvolvimento de modelos de IA para grandes linguagens. A Anthropic busca uma avaliação de mercado de cerca de US$2 trilhões e planeja investir centenas de bilhões nos próximos anos para acelerar seu crescimento. A receita aumentou 12 vezes em 2025, chegando a quase US$4,6 bilhões, enquanto o prejuízo operacional mais que dobrou, ultrapassando US$8 bilhões, informou a Reuters com exclusividade nesta segunda-feira. Os EUA representaram quase dois terços do total das vendas. Aproximadamente US$3,8 bilhões da receita da Anthropic vieram de clientes que pagam com base no uso do sistema de IA Claude, enquanto a receita de assinaturas totalizou US$789 milhões. A Anthropic afirmou que espera que a receita baseada no consumo represente "a grande maioria" de sua receita no futuro próximo. CONCENTRAÇÃO DE RECEITA CRESCE As vendas realizadas por meio dos marketplaces em nuvem totalizaram cerca de US$2,16 bilhões, ou 47% da receita anual da Anthropic em 2025, conforme mostra o documento. De acordo com uma análise da Reuters, a empresa pagou aproximadamente US$351 milhões em taxas de distribuição às plataformas, o que sugere que os provedores de nuvem receberam cerca de 16 centavos para cada dólar dessas vendas. A Anthropic contabiliza as taxas de parceiros de canal na rubrica de despesas operacionais "vendas, marketing e parcerias" em suas demonstrações financeiras. As taxas são um dos aspectos de uma relação financeira cada vez mais circular. A Amazon e o Google investiram dezenas de bilhões de dólares na Anthropic, enquanto a desenvolvedora de IA fez enormes compromissos para comprar capacidade computacional. No final de 2025, a Anthropic tinha US$54,6 bilhões em compromissos irrevogáveis de hospedagem e computação. No início de 2026, seus compromissos totais de longo prazo ultrapassaram US$417 bilhões, abrangendo 3,5 gigawatts de capacidade computacional dedicada. A Anthropic, em seu prospecto, apresentou essas relações como uma vantagem. Afirmou que, ao oferecer seu modelo de IA Claude por meio das plataformas em nuvem da Amazon, do Google e da Microsoft (MSFT.O) , a empresa pode aproveitar suas vastas redes de vendas e alcançar clientes que já usam seus serviços, acelerando a "penetração no mercado em uma escala que acreditamos ser difícil para qualquer organização individual replicar diretamente". Mas a empresa também reconheceu que sua dependência de um número limitado de parceiros e fornecedores "cria dinâmicas complexas que podem gerar conflitos de interesse e afetar negativamente nosso acesso à capacidade computacional". A empresa assinou um acordo de computação em nuvem com a Microsoft em novembro. Os provedores de nuvem também obtêm visibilidade dos preços e termos comerciais da Anthropic, o que pode influenciar suas decisões sobre alocação de recursos computacionais e a agressividade com que vendem seus produtos, segundo o documento. As empresas de nuvem também são clientes da Anthropic, conforme observado. A dependência da Anthropic em relação à Amazon e ao Google aumentou à medida que sua receita disparou. As vendas por meio dessas duas empresas subiram de 11% da receita em 2023 para 32% em 2024 e para quase metade no ano passado. A arrecadação de caixa da empresa também é cada vez mais canalizada por meio desses terceiros, que foram responsáveis pela cobrança de 60% dos US$909 milhões em contas de clientes em aberto no final de 2025, um aumento em relação aos 42% em 2024. A Anthropic alertou que disputas ou atrasos nesse processo podem prejudicar o fluxo de caixa, mesmo que a empresa contrate diretamente com os clientes. Sua base de clientes também é concentrada, com dois clientes não identificados gerando 12% da receita cada um no ano passado. A Anthropic alertou que muitos de seus maiores clientes não estão vinculados a contratos de longo prazo e podem reduzir ou interromper os gastos. Os relacionamentos com a nuvem também complicaram as comparações financeiras com a concorrente OpenAI. A Anthropic contabiliza o valor total dos contratos de marketplace — acordos de venda em que os clientes compram acesso ao Claude por meio do marketplace de um provedor de nuvem — como receita, pois define os preços e fornece o serviço, enquanto registra a comissão das plataformas como custo de marketing. A OpenAI informou a investidores e funcionários que essa abordagem infla a receita declarada da Anthropic em bilhões de dólares, conforme noticiado pela Reuters em junho. Na ocasião, a Anthropic declarou à Reuters que segue as práticas contábeis estabelecidas, reconhecendo a receita bruta por ser a "principal" na transação. (Por Echo Wang e Krystal Hu)

item.title: California governor signs PFAS pesticide tracking bill
item.description: Pesticides containing toxic "forever chemicals" will now be tracked by the state of California, the country's largest producer of agricultural products.
item.dc:creator: Renee Hickman
item.content:encoded: Pesticides containing toxic "forever chemicals" will now be tracked by the state of California , the country's largest producer of agricultural products. The legislation, signed this week by Governor Gavin Newsom, requires the state's Department of Pesticide Regulation to indicate whether agricultural pesticides contain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or PFAS, when reporting their use in a public database. It also requires the department to track PFAS pesticide use trends in the state, where nearly half of the vegetables and more than three-quarters of the fruits and nuts in the US are grown. Environmental advocates hope that better data on use of PFAS and their impacts will ultimately lead to more regulation. "This will give the state the opportunity to start analyzing what's being used, applied where, and how to move forward to get rid of it," said Monica Amarelo, vice president of media relations at the Environmental Working Group, an advocacy group that supported the legislation. Research has linked PFAS exposure to harmful health outcomes including cancer, high cholesterol and immune system effects, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. PFAS chemicals are used in a wide variety of products, including water-repellent clothing, firefighting foam and grease-, water- and oil-resistant products like non-stick cooking utensils. An earlier version of the bill, sponsored by Burbank Democrat Nick Schultz, would have prohibited state regulators from approving new pesticides containing PFAS chemicals. That version, championed by environmental groups, was widely opposed by farm groups in the state. It was scaled back to its current version. Still, Schultz said, the law is "a vital step toward ensuring California's agricultural legacy is defined by health and innovation. Tracking and monitoring is the crucial first step." "You can't fix what you can't see," he said.

item.title: Whistleblower loses fee bid in Walgreens' $4.7 billion settlement with US states
item.description: A federal judge on Tuesday denied a whistleblower's bid to receive a cut of retail pharmacy giant Walgreens' $4.7 billion settlement in 2022 that resolved opioid-related claims by more than two dozen US states.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Tuesday denied a whistleblower's bid to receive a cut of retail pharmacy giant Walgreens' $4.7 billion settlement in 2022 that resolved opioid-related claims by more than two dozen US states. US District Judge Joan Lefkow in Chicago said she did not have authority to order individual states to carve out a portion of the settlements they struck with Walgreens Boots Alliance to give to pharmacist T.J. Novak, who previously collected a $25 million whistleblower award from the federal government in a related Walgreens case. Instead, Novak would have to take his claims to the courts in each state involved in the settlement, Lefkow said. Novak's "demand turns on unsettled questions of the laws of twenty-eight states. With the federal claims gone, those states’ courts should answer them," Lefkow said. Attorneys for Novak and a spokesperson for Walgreens did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The ruling stems from a long-running federal case Novak brought against Walgreens in 2018. Novak alleged Walgreens filled illegal opioid prescriptions and then sought reimbursement from government health programs, including Medicare and Medicaid. The U.S. government joined Novak's case and [USN:FWN3QZ073 TEXT:"reached"] a $300 million settlement with Walgreens, which denied wrongdoing. The accord last year included $150 million tied to Novak’s federal False Claims Act allegations, and Novak said he received a 17.25% share of the funds — more than $25 million — as a whistleblower award. More than two dozen states separately settled opioid-related claims with Walgreens in 2022 for more than $4.7 billion. Novak [USN:L6N3YZ1A5 TEXT:"contended"] that the states' settlement improperly ended his claims under the states' versions of the federal False Claims Act, which allows citizens to sue on the government's behalf and share in any recovery. Virginia had argued that the federal court could not impose a "one-size-fits-all" solution on 28 states. Lefkow found that there was no one answer here that would apply to every state. "What remains would require this court to construe the false claims statutes, opioid-allocation statutes, and consent judgments of twenty-eight states on questions their own courts have not answered," Lefkow said. The case is Novak v. Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc., US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, No. 1:18-cv-05452 For Novak: Michael Rosenblat of Rosenblat Law; and David Chizewer and William Meyers of Goldberg Kohn

item.title: Fujimori dice Congreso Perú pone a prueba su paciencia por falta apoyo a medidas contra delincuencia, El Niño
item.description: La presidenta de Perú, Keiko Fujimori, dijo el martes que el Congreso está "poniendo a prueba" su paciencia por la demora en aprobar poderes legislativos que permitan que el Gobierno dicte medidas contra el crimen y el fenómeno climático de El Niño.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La presidenta de Perú, Keiko Fujimori, dijo el martes que el Congreso está "poniendo a prueba" su paciencia por la demora en aprobar poderes legislativos que permitan que el Gobierno dicte medidas contra el crimen y el fenómeno climático de El Niño. Fujimori afirmó que el pedido fue presentado hace cuatro semanas y que la Cámara de Diputados, el primer filtro dominado por la oposición, está dilatando la decisión que permitiría al Gobierno, entre otras medidas, "incorporar" a los militares a la lucha de la policía contra la ola de delincuencia que afecta al país. "Están poniendo a prueba nuestra paciencia", manifestó en un discurso frente a pobladores de un distrito en el sur de Lima. La mandataria, que asumió a fines de julio, dijo que "con o sin el respaldo del Congreso" aprobará normas contra "estas lacras de la delincuencia" y medidas de prevención frente a El Niño. El Congreso, que retomó este año la bicameralidad después de tres décadas, tiene un Senado cuyo poder está dividido entre partidos que apoyan al Gobierno y otros que se oponen. La cámara de Diputados, en tanto, está dominada por un bloque liderado por el partido de izquierda cuyo candidato perdió frente a Fujimori. En un tono más enérgico, Fujimori dijo que esperará en las próximas horas la decisión del Congreso antes de decretar algunas medidas. "Todo dentro del marco democrático, por supuesto; aquí el único golpe que va haber va ser el golpe contra la criminalidad organizada", advirtió la presidenta.

item.title: Trump set to tout Korean investment in Alaska LNG, other projects, sources say
item.description: President Donald Trump could announce as soon as Wednesday his administration intends to tap South Korea's pledged strategic investment package for about $54 billion to build a liquefied natural gas facility in Alaska and several other major US projects, according to two people familiar with the discussions.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump could announce as soon as Wednesday his administration intends to tap South Korea's pledged strategic investment package for about $54 billion to build a liquefied natural gas facility in Alaska and several other major US projects, according to two people familiar with the discussions. The move would come as part of a flurry of economic and investment announcements ahead of November's midterm elections , as Trump seeks to bolster his administration's economic record to shore up voter support. Trump's overall approval rating sank to 32%, the lowest of his political career, according to a [USN:L6N43U101 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"] this month. Voters have expressed concern about the Iran war and high gasoline prices. Alaska has become a central stage for Republicans battling to maintain control of the US Senate, with many analysts regarding the contest there between incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola as a toss-up. A POTENTIAL SOURCE OF ENERGY FOR ASIA The Alaska LNG project would include a pipeline to transport natural gas from Alaska's North Slope to a liquefaction facility on the state's southern coast, where it could be shipped to Asian markets. It would be the first such US project with direct access to Asia, the fastest-growing market for liquefied natural gas. Japan's two biggest LNG importers, JERA and Tokyo Gas, have signed preliminary deals to buy a combined 2 million metric tons a year from Alaska LNG should it be built. Glenfarne, the project's developer, said in March that it had lined up commitments for 13 million tons a year. To line up financing, it needed agreements for another 3 million tons and to make all commitments binding, the company said. Glenfarne could not immediately be reached for comment. Trump has repeatedly promoted the project as a way to expand US energy exports and strengthen ties with allies including South Korea and Japan. The project has faced years of uncertainty over its cost, financing and commercial viability, including in analysis by the South Korean and Japanese governments. Investment from Seoul would represent a potential source of financing for the project. South Korean and US officials have been working to identify projects for the $350 billion [USN:L1N45E040 TEXT:"strategic investment package"] that Seoul pledged under a trade deal last year. The two sides have discussed Alaska LNG, nuclear power and a gas-fired power project in Texas, among other potential investments. South Korea’s embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Seoul and Washington have been close allies since the 1950-53 Korean War, but there have been [USN:L4N44F04O TEXT:"tensions"] in recent months, with differences over trade and security cooperation and some sharp criticism of Seoul by Trump.

item.title: Trump says he does not know if Iran is going to 'give up yet'
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he does not know if Iran is going to "give up yet" but cast the country as doing "very poorly" in its war with the US.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he does not know if Iran is going to "give up yet" but cast the country as doing "very poorly" in its war with the US . DETAILS AND QUOTES: "I don't know if they are going to give up yet but they'll give up," Trump told reporters. "They are doing very poorly," he added. A US blockade [USN:L6N45K0UX TEXT:"has cut Iran's financial lifeline"] - oil exports, and economic costs of the war have made life tougher for Iranians. Iran's president told the UN General Assembly last week that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure. The rise in oil prices due to the war has also become a major issue for Trump's Republican Party heading into the November US midterm elections . The war has led to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of global supplies of crude oil and LNG before the conflict. Trump has offered [USN:L4N4061X8 TEXT:"shifting goals and timelines"] for the Iran war that began on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have [USN:L1N3ZR14Q TEXT:"killed thousands"] and [USN:L6N3ZY0Q0 TEXT:"displaced millions"].

item.title: Austin Riley's clutch homer lifts Braves over Phillies in Game 1
item.description: ATLANTA -- Austin Riley's three-run homer capped a two-out rally in the eighth inning and lifted the Atlanta Braves to a 5-3 win over the Philadelphia Phillies in a back-and-forth opening game of the best-of-three National League wild-card series Tuesday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ATLANTA -- Austin Riley's three-run homer capped a two-out rally in the eighth inning and lifted the Atlanta Braves to a 5-3 win over the Philadelphia Phillies in a back-and-forth opening game of the best-of-three National League wild-card series Tuesday afternoon. After Michael Harris II singled and Ozzie Albies was hit by a pitch, Riley lifted the first pitch he saw from Phillies closer Jhoan Duran 385 feet to right-center, putting the Braves ahead with his sixth career postseason homer. "It felt good, no doubt," Riley said. "Just trying to get something over the plate. Duran is a really good pitcher. He's got some really good stuff." Riley posted career lows in batting average (.219), on-base percentage (.290) and slugging percentage (.364) during the regular season, but the eight-year veteran put those struggles behind him with one swing. "Everybody knows kind of how my season went; not the way I wanted it to," Riley said. "But that's the beauty of the postseason. You kind of get a clean slate and go out there and try to do something for the boys and for this city. It's definitely a good start." Duran (0-1), who converted 33 of 35 save opportunities in the regular season, retired the first five batters he faced before yielding the Braves' three-run uprising. "Any time you lose a game late, obviously it's frustrating," said Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly. "But in our minds, we had our best guy out there. You live with this one." Braves closer Raisel Iglesias allowed a leadoff single in the ninth, but he induced a 6-4-3 double play by Bryan De La Cruz and ended the game with a Bryson Stott flyout to record the save. Braves left-hander Dylan Lee (1-0) earned the win with a scoreless eighth. Harris was 3-for-3 and scored two runs for Atlanta, which has a chance on Wednesday afternoon to clinch its first postseason series win since the 2021 World Series. J.T. Realmuto delivered a two-out, two-run triple in the top of the seventh to give the Phillies a 3-2 lead. Alec Bohm contributed an RBI double for Philadelphia, which was held to six hits and went 1-for-5 with runners in scoring position. Braves starter Chris Sale was in line for the loss as he allowed two baserunners in the seventh before Didier Fuentes surrendered Realmuto's triple. Making his first postseason start since 2021, Sale struck out a playoff career-high nine. He gave up three runs on four hits and walked one over 6 1/3 innings. Phillies left-hander Jesus Luzardo -- making his first start in three weeks after a late-season stint on the injured list due to shoulder inflammation -- also delivered as the Game 1 starter. He allowed one run on three hits over five innings, striking out six and walking one. Bohm gave the Phillies the lead four batters into the game when he doubled into the left center gap to bring home Kyle Schwarber, who had walked. The Braves leveled the score in the second when Mike Yastrzemski rolled a seeing-eye single up the middle to plate Albies after Mauricio Dubon's leadoff double to left ignited the rally. In the sixth, Atlanta took advantage of Luzardo's exit. Albies' RBI triple to right center off Alex McFarlane drove in Harris to forge a 2-1 lead. --Curt Weiler, Field Level Media

item.title: Lamine nets double as Spain win again and England beat 10-man Czechs
item.description: Lamine Yamal scored twice as World Cup winners Spain extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches and maintained their perfect start to Nations League Group A3 with a 4-1 home win over Croatia on Tuesday, while England overcame 10-man Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamine Yamal scored twice as World Cup winners Spain extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches and maintained their perfect start to Nations League Group A3 with a 4-1 home win over Croatia on Tuesday, while England overcame 10-man Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague. In a repeat of the 2023 Nations League final, which Spain won on penalties, Croatia recovered from conceding an early goal to equalise but were unable to resist a Spanish side fresh from a 3-2 win over England at Wembley on Saturday. Spain's first home game since lifting the World Cup in July was preceded by Rodri parading the trophy on the pitch and the celebrations continued in Seville when Lamine, just as he did against England, opened the scoring in the second minute. Alex Baena's ball into the area was dummied by Fermin Lopez and Lamine curled a first-time low shot inside the far post. Baena then had an effort parried away by Croatia keeper Dominik Livakovic as Spain looked set to put the game out of reach early on but the visitors drew level through Dion Beljo's 28th-minute header. Spain took less than three minutes to retake the lead. Lamine whipped a cross into the six-yard box from the right wing and Marc Pubill powered a header beyond Livakovic. Lamine scored his second and Spain's third in the 63rd minute, collecting Pedri's pass in the box before drilling his shot into the net from a tight angle, and substitute Nico Williams wrapped up the win with an 89th-minute goal. "He's a special player," Williams told Teledeporte about Lamine. GORDON AND KANE DOWN CZECHS England struggled to find a way past the Czechs in the opening half, even with a numerical advantage, but an early second-half goal from Anthony Gordon sent Thomas Tuchel's side on their way. Morgan Rogers hit the post and Elliot Anderson's goalbound follow-up shot was blocked by defender Robin Hranac before England's chances were boosted by a red card for the hosts, with Pavel Sulc given his marching orders for a foul on Anderson in the 23rd minute. "Strange to get an early red card, not the best for the team and spectators," England manager Thomas Tuchel told ITV. "It's an awkward one but we kept going, got a win and that's what counts." The Czechs had shown plenty of early promise before the sending off, but then sat back and England failed to create much real danger until taking the lead two minutes after the break. Trent Alexander-Arnold, making his first England start in almost two years and just his second appearance under Tuchel, floated the ball into the box and Gordon stooped to guide a header into the bottom corner. "I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass," Gordon said. Gordon nearly turned provider minutes later with a cutback for Lewis Hall, but the England defender dragged his shot wide. Hall then played a cross into the box which Czech captain Ladislav Krejci almost turned into his own net, with the ball hitting the upright, but England found the second goal in the 69th minute. Harry Kane was in the right place at the right time to pounce on a loose ball in the area to sweep his strike into the far corner. England had chances to increase their lead late on, with Eberechi Eze denied by the keeper, while Alex Scott almost marked his debut in style after coming off the bench, but his effort, after a one-two with Eze, went wide. In Group B1, Scotland suffered a 3-0 home loss to Switzerland after going down to 10 men in the 11th minute. Jack Hendry was sent off for a foul on Dan Ndoye and from the resulting free kick, Ricardo Rodriguez whipped the ball into the far corner. Ndoye provided the assists for both Nico Elvedi and Zeki Amdouni's second-half goals as the Swiss made it two wins from two. In the group's other match, Slovenia beat North Macedonia 2-0.

item.title: トランプ氏、8.5兆円規模のアラスカLNG計画発表へ－中間選挙苦戦の中
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は、韓国による約2000億ドル（約31兆4600億円）の対米投資計画を発表する見通しだ。この中には、長年停滞しているアラスカ産天然ガスの輸出を目指す事業への540億ドル（約8兆4900億円）の投資が含まれる。同事業は、再選を狙い接戦となっている共和党上院議員が推進してきた。

事情に詳しい複数の関係者が匿名を条件に明らかにしたところでは、今回発表される計画は、昨年の米韓貿易合意に基づき支援対象となる事業の第1弾となる。同合意には、3500億ドルの対米投資を行うとの約束が盛り込まれていた。関係者によると、トランプ氏は30日、大統領執務室で発表する見通しだ。

韓国の支援は、アラスカ州内を横断して天然ガスを輸送し、その大半をアジアの買い手に輸出する同事業の開発に不可欠となる公算が大きい。事情に詳しい関係者によれば、原子力事業を含む他のエネルギー事業にも韓国からの投資の一部が振り向けられる見通しだ。

非公開企業の米グレンファーン・グループがアラスカLNG事業を開発している。同事業はこれまでにLNG輸入業者と予備的な合意を結んでいるものの、最終投資決定には至っていない。同社はコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

今回の発表の計画は、11月の中間選挙を前に、経済を巡る有権者の不満を背景に強い逆風に直面する共和党候補を後押しするため、トランプ氏が大統領としての権限と国際的なディール外交を活用する新たな事例となる。

アラスカ州選出の共和党のサリバン上院議員は、以前からアラスカLNG事業を強く支持。再選を目指して、民主党のペルトラ元下院議員と争っている。

関係者の話では、サリバン氏は30日の発表に合わせてホワイトハウスを訪れ、同州選出の共和党のベギッチ下院議員とダンリービー州知事も同席する予定。サリバン氏の事務所にコメントを要請したものの、返答は得られていない。

原題：Trump to Tout $54 Billion Alaska LNG Plan Amid Midterm Woes (1)（抜粋）

item.title: Trading Day: Stocks still in bonds' grip
item.description: US and world stocks slipped for a second day on Tuesday, pressured by elevated bond yields, and investor jitters around US inflation figures and potential quarter-end volatility on Wednesday. Bearish sentiment was tempered by falling oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
US and world [USN:L4N45L0MW TEXT:"stocks slipped"] for a second day on Tuesday, pressured by elevated bond yields, and investor jitters around US inflation figures and potential quarter-end volatility on Wednesday. Bearish sentiment was tempered by falling oil prices. In [USN:L6N45K13P TEXT:"my column today"], I look at the cracks that are beginning to appear in the AI financing edifice. Bonds issued to fund data center construction are coming under heavy pressure - but is this a warning of more turbulence ahead, or a 'buy' signal? Today's Key Reads [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"EXCLUSIVE-Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows sweeping AI vision, surging costs"] [USN:L1N45K0VR TEXT:"Trump says working with Xi on AI would hurt US companies"] [USN:L6N45K107 TEXT:"'G force' driving world markets may need Fed and bond brake: Mike Dolan"] [USN:L1N45K0MU TEXT:"Battered bond market braces for a new era of interest rates"] [USN:P8N44P09G TEXT:"China unveils rate cut, mortgage subsidies to spur growth"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Japan -0.6%, [USN:L6N45L0EA TEXT:"Europe"] flat, [USN:L6N45L0IN TEXT:"UK"] -0.5%. Nasdaq -0.1%, S&P 500 -0.2%, Dow -0.3%. SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 fall, four rise. Energy -0.9%, utilities +1.1%. US chip sector +1.3%. [USN:L4N45L1G6 TEXT:"Apple"] biggest loser on the Dow, -2.7%. [USN:L6N45L0TG TEXT:"Carnival"] biggest gainer on the S&P 500, +13%. FX: [USN:L4N45L03Z TEXT:"Dollar"] +0.3%, strongest in 2 months. Aussie dollar -0.7% after [USN:P8N3X1041 TEXT:"RBA"] hike, Norwegian krone -1%. BONDS: Selloff pauses in UK and Europe, although French-German spread posts widest close in 14 years. US 30-year yield 5.62%, highest since 2002. Entire US curve within 5 bps of trading above 5%. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N45K1PF TEXT:"Oil"] -2.5%, [USN:L4N45L01H TEXT:"gold"] +1% .

Today's Talking Points: Anthropicology The [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"Reuters exclusive"] report on Anthropic's propsoed IPO makes for fascinating reading. The AI giant's revenue grew 12-fold last year, but losses exceeded $8 billion on an operating basis and more than $40 billion on a net basis, according to the prospectus documents for a prospective IPO that is targeting a valuation of more than $2 trillion. Essentially, the company is spending big, and losing money. Or it has been until now. The hope is that revenues continue to grow at an ever-increasing rate, overtaking the huge spend, and justifying the eye-popping IPO [USN:L4N45L180 TEXT:"valuation"]. But the threat of cheaper Chinese models looms large. Anthropic's costs and investment outlays mean it might struggle in a price war, if it comes to that. Consumer blues It's a conundrum. The US economy is expanding at an annual pace of around 8% to 9% in nominal terms, and the unemployment rate is 4.1%, a historically low rate essentially reflecting full employment. Yet Americans are gloomier than they have been in years. [USN:AQN2MLCVJ TEXT:"Consumer confidence"] slumped this month to the lowest since 2014, and are more insecure about the jobs market than they have been in more than five years. What gives? Consumer confidence has for years been a poor leading indicator of consumer behavior, and by extension, wider economic growth. Spending has held up, thanks to robust spending by the wealthy, growth is strong and corporate profits and stock prices have never been higher. Maybe a "mean reversion" is overdue? No quarter given A tumultuous third quarter draws to a close on Wednesday, a three-month period that saw, in no particular order: a 40% rebound in oil, record US diesel prices, the biggest quarterly slump in corporate bonds since 2022, a crashing wave of AI "doomerism," the Fed raise interest rates and US and global government bond yields hit their highest in 20 years. Oh, and in among all that, stocks hit record highs. It will be difficult for the fourth quarter to be as seismic, but investors should buckle up. Worries over AI - financial, and its existential threat to humanity - are only likely to deepen; the Fed is on track to continue its tightening cycle; US midterm elections are looming; and the US war on Iran is still raging. Can equities shrug all that off again? The third-quarter earnings season that kicks into gear in the next few weeks will be revealing. What could move markets tomorrow? They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル上昇、米金利高が支援 対ユーロで16カ月ぶり高値
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ２９日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場で、ドルが主要通貨に対して上昇し、対ユーロと対スイスフランで...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル上昇、米金利高が支援　対ユーロで16カ月ぶり高値 5:54 配信

２０１１年１１月撮影　 REUTERS/Kacper Pempel

［ニューヨーク　２９日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場で、ドルが主要通貨に対して上昇し、対ユーロと対スイスフランで１年４カ月ぶりの高値を付けた。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が追加利上げに動くか見極めようと一連の米経済指標が注目される中、米国債利回りが数年ぶりの高水準近辺で推移していることがドルの下支えになっている。

ドル／円はほぼ横ばいの１５７．３０円近辺。片山さつき財務相は２９日の閣議後会見で、今後の為替政策について「引き続き日米当局の間で緊密なコミュニケーションを維持し、秩序ある為替市場の維持に取り組む」と発言。市場では日米の協調介入の可能性を探る動きが出ている。

ユーロに対しては世界的なエネルギーショックのほか、欧州の政治リスクの高まりが重石になっており、ユーロ／ドル は一時１．１３１２ドルと、２０２５年５月以来の安値を付けた。終盤の取引では０．２６％安の１．１３４１ドル。

この日は米１０年債利回りが２００７年６月以来の高水準を付け、５％を上回って推移。ドル相場を下支えした。コーペイのチーフ市場ストラテジスト、カール・シャモッタ氏は「金利差の拡大が為替市場の主な動意になる中、ドルは主要通貨全般に対して上昇している」と指摘。マネーコープのトレーディング・ストラクチャード商品部門責任者、ユージン・エプスタイン氏は「現在は個々の経済指標を見極めている段階だ」とし、「雇用と物価の指標を精査し、ＦＲＢ当局者が示唆しているタカ派姿勢が正当化されるか判断しようとしている」と述べた。

連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者の間では、バー理事がＦＲＢが目標とする２％のインフレ率に向けた進展が「軌道から外れた」とし、追加利上げの必要性を改めて訴えた。一方、ニューヨーク連銀のウィリアムズ総裁は、ＦＲＢは９月の会合で利上げを決定したため、現在は性急に行動する必要はないとの考えを示し、今後発表される経済指標を見極めてから次の対応を決定することで経済がどのような状況にあるのかより明確に把握できると発言。１０月２７─２８日の次回ＦＯＭＣでの追加利上げ観測の後退につながった。

ドルは対スイスフランで０．１７％高の０．８３４フラン。

主要６通貨に対するドル指数は０．２％高の１０１．４０と、７月２８日以来の水準を更新した。

ドル／円　ＮＹ終値 157.28/157.31

始値 157.20

高値 157.69

安値 156.99

ユーロ／ドル　ＮＹ終値 1.1340/1.1344

始値 1.1348

高値 1.1358

安値 1.1313
